items.title: Malaysian lorry driver arrested in Singapore over 800 cartons of smuggled cigarettes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 33-year-old Malaysian lorry driver was arrested after Singapore authorities discovered more than 800 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden beneath baskets of vegetables in his vehicle at the Woodlands Checkpoint. The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), in a Facebook post, said the smuggling attempt was foiled on Oct 8. It added that during the checks, more than 800 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes were uncovered hidden beneath baskets of vegetables in white trash bags, the authority said.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH aims to defend seats, eyes fresh gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) aims to defend its existing seats while looking to capture several target seats through strategic efforts in the upcoming Melaka state election. PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said their baseline is to retain the seats they hold. On Saturday, PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the coalition would contest 21 seats in the Melaka state election next month.

items.title: Asean envoy to visit Myanmar Wednesday - Thai FM
items.summary: BANGKOK: Asean's special envoy for Myanmar, Philippines Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro, will visit Naypyidaw on Wednesday and Thursday, her Thai counterpart said. Asean chair the Philippines had earlier this year requested "brief access" for its envoy to Suu Kyi, but was rebuffed. Sihasak said Lazaro's visit was timed to allow the envoy to report back to a meeting of Asean ministers ahead of a leaders summit.

items.title: [UPDATED] Police probe Noorizwan custodial death as grievous hurt to obtain confession
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have reclassified the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly while in custody at the Cheras district police for voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort a confession. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the case was reclassified after a forensic expert confirmed that injuries found on Noorizwan's body were consistent with blunt force trauma and were not self-inflicted. He said Bukit Aman's Prosecution and Legal Division (D5) had taken over investigations into the Oct 1 custodial death.

items.title: Immigration arrests 71 in passport forgery crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has arrested 71 people in 17 enforcement operations since 2024 in a crackdown on syndicates accused of falsifying passports to help foreign workers undergo mandatory medical examinations using other people's identities. It said intelligence gathering and enforcement operations since 2024 had uncovered syndicates involved in falsifying passports and altering personal information to help foreign workers undergo medical examinations using other people's identities. The syndicates' modus operandi involved replacing passport photographs and altering personal details to help foreign workers undergo medical examinations using another person's identity, the department said.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Tuesday, Oct 27, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1564947]] [[nid:1564946]] [[nid:1564945]] [[nid:1564944]] [[nid:1564943]] [[nid:1564942]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Defence Ministry holds mental well-being programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: About 300 military and civilian personnel attended the Defence Ministry's Psychology Open Day to promote mental well-being, emotional resilience and a healthier workplace. The sales activities provided additional engagement opportunities for personnel attending the programme. Participants had access to psychological support services, health screenings and financial advice from eight participating agencies.

items.title: YNH unit settles LHDN tax dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: YNH Property Bhd's unit, YNH Construction Sdn Bhd has reached a settlement with the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN), paving the way for the withdrawal of a winding-up petition filed against it in March 2026. YNH Property said at the High Court hearing on July 16 this year, no winding-up order was made against YNH Construction. YNH Property said it would provide further updates on any material developments through the appropriate disclosure channels.

items.title: China still tops list of international students in Malaysia, but other markets are growing, says EMGS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — While China remains Malaysia’s largest source of international students, the Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) said applications from other countries are growing. EMGS chairman Datuk Ahmad Shalimin Ahmad Shaffie said China accounted for approximately 41 per cent of applications in 2023, but the proportion has since declined as Malaysia attracts students from more markets. Ahmad Shalimin said regional figures further reflected this growing diversity.

items.title: HB Global unable to meet FY26 annual report deadline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HB Global Ltd will be unable to issue its annual report, comprising the annual audited financial statements and the auditors' and directors' reports for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), by Oct 30, 2026. The deadline is prescribed under Paragraph 9.23(1) of Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd's Main Market Listing Requirements (MMLR). Following the decision, HB Global remains subject to the Oct 30, 2026 deadline to issue its annual report.

items.title: Hong Leong Bank, Unionpay partner to facilitate cross-border payments in China
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Bank Bhd's (HLB) customers can now make QR payments at more than 120 million UnionPay and Weixin Pay merchant touchpoints across China through the HLB Connect application, following a strategic partnership with UnionPay International (UPI). HLB group managing director and chief executive officer Kevin Lam said the collaboration would provide Malaysian travellers with greater convenience and confidence when making payments overseas, while laying the foundation for wider payment connectivity in other markets. Lam said the partnership leveraged UPI's international network, including Weixin Pay, to provide customers with access to a wider merchant network directly through the banking application they already use in Malaysia.

items.title: Kulasegaran declines update on Teoh Beng Hock private prosecution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran has declined to give an update on the possibility of a private prosecution in the Teoh Beng Hock case. He said the matter falls under the Attorney-General's Chambers and the police. He said his portfolio covered amending laws, but the case was outside that scope.

items.title: RM270k in Budi Madani subsidies withheld over suspected abuse
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: More than RM270,000 in subsidy payments to a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, Penang, have been withheld after it was suspected of abusing the Budi Madani programme. The ministry said it acted after Budi Madani recipients discovered that their MyKad details had been used without their knowledge to buy subsidised petrol. Budi Madani is the government's targeted fuel subsidy programme, while Budi95 specifically covers subsidised RON95 petrol.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 27, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Rosmah faces bankruptcy Global Royalty Trading will enforce a RM67.5 million judgment against Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor over 43 missing pieces of jewellery. Family seeks answers The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died in police custody, wants MPs to raise the case in Parliament. Anwar bars politicians Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says politicians cannot decide projects or priorities for GLICs and GLCs.

items.title: First the floods, then the heat: MetMalaysia warns of challenging months ahead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Malaysia may experience hotter and drier weather towards the end of the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL), especially from late January to March next year, following expectations of a Super El Niño phenomenon that could lead to reduced rainfall across the country Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said these conditions could increase the risk of heatwaves and droughts, especially if rainfall decreases during that period. He said the El Niño phenomenon is currently in a strong phase and is expected to intensify to a very strong level or Super El Niño towards the end of this year and into next year. “With reduced rainfall, hot weather or heatwaves often emerge, along with drought due to water shortages caused by insufficient rainfall,” he said as a guest on Bernama TV’s “Fokus 15” programme today.

items.title: Agoda, Adyen explore new payment services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Agoda and financial technology platform Adyen are exploring cooperation in payment issuing and payouts in selected markets, as the online travel platform looks to expand its payment capabilities. Adyen now provides payment acquiring services for Agoda across multiple regions, supporting a range of local payment methods and currencies. Their efforts include integrating local payment options, simplifying authentication for legitimate bookings and optimising payment routing to improve transaction reliability.

items.title: Maritime officer killed, three injured during pursuit of suspected migrant boat off Perlis
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 27 — A Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) personnel was killed and three others injured when their boat collided with a concrete structure during an enforcement operation off Kuala Sungai Padang, Kuala Perlis, last night. Kedah and Perlis Maritime director First Admiral Romli Mustafa said five MMEA personnel were conducting the operation at 11.37pm to intercept a boat suspected of carrying undocumented Myanmar migrants. He said the suspected migrant boat sped towards the shore after being detected, triggering a 15-minute pursuit.

items.title: BMS Holdings expands northern reach with JV
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: BMS Holdings Bhd has formed a joint venture with Wee Tatt Traders Sdn Bhd and its shareholders to expand its presence in the northern region of Peninsular Malaysia. The joint venture will be undertaken through Jubin BMS (Wee Tatt) Sdn Bhd, which is 60 per cent-owned by BMS Holdings and 40 per cent by Wee Tatt's shareholders. The partners will contribute a total of RM5 million to the joint venture, comprising RM3 million in cash from BMS Holdings and RM2 million in inventory from Wee Tatt's shareholders.

items.title: MMEA sailor killed off Perlis was devoted to duty, wife says
items.summary: ALOR STAR: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer killed in a boat collision off Perlis last night was deeply committed to his duties, his wife said. Sajaratul Akmal Abdul Shukor, 41, said her husband, Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, was always ready to serve regardless of the time or weather, even reporting for duty on his days off. "He loved his job and would report for duty even on his days off.

items.title: Bintai Kinden wins RM20.3mil TNB contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bintai Kinden Corporation Bhd has secured a RM20.28 million contract from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to extend two transformers at a substation in Pahang. The mechanical and electrical engineering services provider said the project involves extending two transformers at the PMU Avetani substation, with completion expected within 540 days from the commencement date. The contract brings the company's outstanding order book to RM183.8 million, providing earnings visibility in the near term.

items.title: UMPSA to publish book on SMA scholar Siti Hawa
items.summary: KUANTAN: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) will publish a book documenting the life and struggles of Dr Siti Hawa Apandi, who died today. Vice-Chancellor Professor Ts Dr Yatimah Alias said the book would chronicle the spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) patient's journey, from her diploma studies in 2007 to completing her PhD last year. "The book is being prepared with contributions from Siti Hawa's supervisors and UMPSA's Centre for Inclusive Technology and Ecosystem," she said today.

items.title: Lawyers must not rely blindly on AI, says Kulasegaran
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lawyers must never rely blindly on information generated by artificial intelligence, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran. "Such incidents remind us that lawyers must never rely blindly on AI generated information," he said at the launch of LAWYes, an artificial intelligence platform for legal practice, here today. He said discussions on artificial intelligence in the legal profession must always be linked to service quality, responsibility and public trust.

items.title: More than 10,000 visitors expected at National Deepavali celebration in Brickfields on Nov 14
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — More than 10,000 visitors are expected at the National Deepavali Celebration organised by the National Unity Ministry (KPN) in Brickfields here on November 14. Deputy Minister R. Yuneswaran said the event, expected to be officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, would feature arts, culture and heritage activities from morning until night, including performances by artistes and unique exhibitions such as Rumah Malaysia. Yuneswaran called on media practitioners to work with the ministry and relevant departments to promote unity and social harmony, urging them to move away from issues related to the 3Rs (race, religion and royalty) or anything that could undermine social harmony.

items.title: Zetrix AI stages 13.3pct rebound
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd shares rebounded 13.33 per cent to close at 8.5 sen amid speculative buying today, following months of heavy selling. Prior to today's movement, forced selling from margin calls and an aggressive credit rating downgrade to junk status by MARC Ratings had wiped out over 90 per cent of Zetrix AI's market value. An observer said the 13.33 per cent bounce is heavily technical, driven by speculative traders targeting a severely beaten-down stock.

items.title: Govt explores ways to sustain airlines, maintain connectivity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is exploring ways to help airlines remain sustainable and ensure connectivity is maintained, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. "We are trying to ensure the aviation industry is sustainable, and the government's priority is to ensure connectivity continues. Loke said the government's priority was to keep national airlines operating, as the collapse of any major airline would affect connectivity.

items.title: Bukit Dinding set to become permanent forest reserve by November
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The gazettement of Bukit Dinding as a Permanent Forest Reserve is now at its final stage, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui. He said the application to revoke the reservation of the open space at the site had been approved by the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Working Committee, while the gazettement process is expected to be completed by the end of November. He said the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Lands and Mines Office director would prepare a draft gazette for the revocation of the open space reservation for review by the Attorney-General's Chambers before submitting it to the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Working Committee meeting chairman for signing, after which it would be published by Percetakan Nasional Malaysia Berhad.

items.title: Election Commission to set key dates for Sarawak polls on Nov 6
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 27 — The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on November 6 to discuss key dates for the 13th Sarawak state election. He said the EC had today received official notification from Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar confirming the dissolution of the 19th Sarawak State Legislative Assembly, effective yesterday, in accordance with Article 21(2) of the State Constitution. “Under Article 21(4) of the Sarawak State Constitution, an election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution,” he said.

items.title: After five years and 38 witnesses, prosecution closes case in Lim Guan Eng trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — After more than five years of proceedings and calling 38 witnesses, the prosecution today closed its case in the RM6.3 billion undersea tunnel and major roads project corruption trial involving former Penang chief minister Lim Guan Eng. I hereby close the prosecution’s case and offer Penang Mayor Datuk Rajendran P. Anthony to the defence should they be called to enter their defence,” he said. Among the key witnesses called were former Consortium Zenith Construction Sdn Bhd director Datuk Zarul Ahmad Mohd Zulkifli, former Penang state executive councillor Datuk Lim Hock Seng, former Penang state secretary Datuk Seri Farizan Darus, former tourism and culture minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Nazri Abdul Aziz, and businessman Datuk Seri G. Gnanaraja.

items.title: Super El Nino: Hotter, drier weather in Malaysia from late Jan-March
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia may experience hotter and drier weather towards the end of the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon, especially from late January to March next year. This is as the Super El Nino phenomenon could lead to reduced rainfall across the country Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said these conditions could increase the risk of heatwaves and droughts, especially if rainfall decreases during that period. "With reduced rainfall, hot weather or heatwaves often emerge, along with drought due to water shortages caused by insufficient rainfall," he said as a guest on Bernama TV's "Fokus 15" programme.

items.title: Infomina bags contract for National Registration Dept's app systems
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd has secured a RM32.11 million contract from the Home Ministry to provide maintenance and technical support services for the National Registration Department's (NRD) core application systems. The contract, worth RM32.11 million excluding service tax, covers system maintenance, technical support, data and file management, user training, technical courses and review workshops. Infomina said the contract is expected to contribute positively to its earnings over the contract period.

items.title: Dataprep executive chairman Wan Ahmad Rudirman resigns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dataprep Holdings Bhd has announced the resignation of its executive chairman, Dr Wan Ahmad Rudirman Wan Razak. Wan Ahmad Rudirman was redesignated from managing director to executive chairman of the company on Aug 4, 2026. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Police detain four Myanmar boys after elderly woman reports intimidation
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 27 — Police detained four Myanmar boys to assist in investigations into a criminal intimidation case involving an elderly woman in Taman Sri Rambai here, an incident which has also gone viral on social media. Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT) police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said all four children, aged between nine and 12, were detained in separate raids around the area following a police report lodged by the 71-year-old victim yesterday. Nik Aminuddin added that police seized several exhibits believed to be connected to the incident, and all four suspects have been remanded for four days until October 30 to facilitate investigations.

items.title: Anwar vows tough action against migrant smuggling syndicates
items.summary: This follows the death of Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency intelligence officer Leading Seaman (Technical) Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, who was killed while trying to stop the entry of undocumented migrants. "The lives of security personnel and the nation's sovereignty must not be gambled with," Anwar said in a social media post today. He said he was deeply affected by Roshaimi's death and disappointed by the actions of those who threatened the nation's security and sovereignty.

items.title: Ni Hsin proposes bonus issue of up to 312.65mil warrants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd has proposed a bonus issue of up to 312.65 million warrants on the basis of one warrant for every two existing ordinary shares held by entitled shareholders. Proceeds raised from the exercise of the warrants will be utilised for Ni Hsin's working capital and capital expenditure. The company said the proceeds are expected to be fully utilised within 24 months from the date of receipt of the funds.

items.title: HSBC profits surge by a third as cost-cutting exceeds target
items.summary: LONDON: HSBC has revealed its quarterly profits have leapt by nearly a third as it nears the end of a US$2 billion cost-cutting programme, reported PA Media/dpa. HSBC also announced it would be handing up to US$1 billion to shareholders as part of a new share buyback scheme. HSBC said it had beaten this target with cost savings worth US$1.9 billion, which it expects to reach US$2 billion by the end of the year.

items.title: TuJu not designed to compete with Waze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The TuJu navigation app was never intended to compete with Waze, Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) chairman Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad said. He said TuJu was developed with private app developers to upgrade MHA's Traffic Management Centre. Hasni said TuJu operated only on toll and federal highways and was still under development.

items.title: Penang CM Chow says developer and landowner must answer for fatal Paya Terubong landslide
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 27 — The landowner and developer of a condominium and road construction project on a hillside near the landslide site in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, must take responsibility and ensure the safety of the affected area, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said. He said the parties involved must be held accountable, particularly as the landslide, which claimed the life of a doctor, occurred on land owned by the developer. Chow said the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had issued an immediate stop-work order and given the developer seven days to submit a mitigation plan to address safety risks at the site.

items.title: Eco-Shop posts higher Q1 FY27 net profit of RM63.19mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd's net profit for the first quarter of financial year 2027 ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q1 FY27) rose by 7.6 per cent to RM63.19 million from RM58.75 million posted in Q1 FY26. Revenue also jumped by 16 per cent to RM793.67 million from RM684.33 million in the previous corresponding quarter. Ng said that after opening 100 new stores in the previous financial year, Eco-Shop is targeting another 100 new store openings in FY2027.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: RM14.3m returned to online scam victims, RM100.9m losses prevented
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) has recovered and returned RM14.3 million to online scam victims between Oct 12, 2022 and September this year. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the NSRC had also prevented losses amounting to RM100.93 million, while losses reported through its 997 hotline totalled RM1.2 billion from 468,675 calls received between Oct 12, 2022 and August this year. Saifuddin Nasution said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continued to intensify intelligence gathering and joint operations to combat organised crime syndicates using Malaysia as a base for their operations.

items.title: Wee Ka Siong says too early to call MCA-Barisan talks on Melaka seats ‘positive’
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 27 — MCA has yet to reach a decision on its position in the Melaka state election, with party president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong saying it is still too early to describe ongoing discussions with Barisan Nasional over seat allocations as having produced a positive outcome. In a Facebook post today, Wee said MCA had conveyed its dissatisfaction over the allocation of seats for the Melaka polls during a meeting with Barisan leaders late on Monday. MCA clearly expressed our dissatisfaction with the seat allocation for the Melaka state election.

items.title: Fix your water supply before chasing RM720b GDP dream, Akmal tells SG4 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Chronic deficits in basic utilities, highlighted by Kedah's zero per cent water reserve margin, will derail the ambitious long-term economic targets set by the four opposition-led SG4 states, Economy Minister Akmal Nasir warned today. Federal development expenditure in the four states reached RM7.70 billion in 2025, approximately 6.8 times their combined state development allocations of roughly RM1.13 billion. Addressing commercial inflows, Akmal cited Malaysian Investment Development Authority data recording RM37.23 billion in approved investments and 18,319 potential jobs across the four states in 2025.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Health Service Commission Bill to be tabled by end of 15th Parliament if approved
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to obtain a policy decision from the Cabinet on the establishment of the Health Service Commission (SPK) this year and, if approved, table the Bill in Parliament by the end of the 15th Parliament at the latest. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the establishment of the commission would further strengthen the management of human resources and the welfare of healthcare personnel, covering all 86 service schemes under the MOH. “These are among our efforts to improve matters while moving towards the establishment of a Health Service Commission, as envisaged in the White Paper by the Health Reform Commission,” he said.

items.title: Govt initiates legal action against Zetrix AI over unpaid JPJ revenue, rejected RM231m cheque
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is taking civil legal action against collection agent Zetrix AI Berhad after the company failed to remit millions in government revenue collected on behalf of the Road Transport Department (JPJ). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the legal action followed the company’s failure to settle its total outstanding balance and accrued late-payment penalties within the stipulated deadline. JPJ subsequently lodged a police report on October 7 over the unremitted government revenue.

items.title: Johor man with six previous criminal and drug-related offences arrested over axe murder of 68-year-old Felda settler
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 27 — Police arrested a 41-year-old man suspected of hacking a settler to death with an axe at Felda Lok Heng Selatan last night. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect was arrested by a joint team from the state contingent and district police at a palm oil plantation here at 10.26am today. “Police seized a motorcycle and an axe from the suspect.

items.title: ‘Betrayal’: Putrajaya cuts off Penang petrol station over suspected Budi Madani subsidy abuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Putrajaya has cut off a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, Penang, from the Budi Madani fuel subsidy over suspected misuse that allegedly involved customers’ MyKad details being used without their knowledge. It has barred the station from selling subsidised RON95 and diesel under Budi Madani. It did not name the petrol station.

items.title: Nik Nazmi spends four hours at Jais, now waits to hear if he will be charged
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 27 — Bersama co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad spent more than four hours at the Selangor Islamic Religious Department here today, giving his statement over the khalwat case. That decision, he said, rests with the Selangor Syariah Prosecution Department. He said statements from Nik Nazmi and the woman linked to the case were taken separately.

items.title: LPT3 highway from Terengganu to Kelantan to proceed via competitive bidding, says Nanta
items.summary: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the proposed alignment, stretching from Kampung Gemuruh in Terengganu to Tunjong in Kelantan, would complement LPT1 and LPT2 in connecting Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan. Nanta said the government’s current priority was to ensure that the Central Spine Road (LTU) and Kota Bharu-Kuala Krai Highway (KBKK) projects progressed smoothly and were completed on schedule. For the 70.4-kilometre KBKK project, he said overall physical progress had reached 78.80 per cent, with the Pasir Hor-Kadok stretch fully completed.

items.title: Pahang allocates RM3.78m for monsoon preparations, sends aid supplies to 167 forward bases
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 27 — The Pahang state government has allocated more than RM3 million to prepare for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), including the early delivery of aid supplies to 167 forward bases statewide. Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government, through the Pahang Social Welfare Department (JKM), had coordinated a total allocation of RM3,785,115.30 for dry food supplies, logistics, transportation and labour costs across 11 districts. He said 332,906 units of dry food supplies, comprising nine basic food items weighing a total of 225.11 tonnes, would be distributed to the forward bases from today until Nov 14.

items.title: Crocodile snatches 13-year-old in Sarawak, rescue teams launch search
items.summary: The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said it was notified of the incident at around 7pm. Bomba Sarawak said Simunjan fire station personnel are currently at the scene conducting a search and rescue (SAR) operation for the boy. In a Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunters Sarawak Crocter said the attack occurred at around 4pm when the victim was loading oil palm fruits into a boat.

items.title: Nearly 72pc of major hospitals record bed waiting times under eight hours, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: As of June 2026, 28 of the country’s 39 Type 1 and Type 2 hospitals, or 71.8 per cent, recorded average waiting times of less than eight hours for admission from Emergency Departments. These hospitals include state hospitals and major specialist hospitals that handle high numbers of emergency patients and referrals from surrounding districts. Dzulkefly added that 94 of 103 Type 3 and Type 4 hospitals (91.3 per cent), including minor specialist hospitals and hospitals without specialists, had average bed waiting times under four hours.

items.title: Ramanan: More funding being considered for Uyarvu Madani to help small Indian entrepreneurs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 27 — The government, through the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA), will consider applying for additional funding to expand assistance to small entrepreneurs, particularly those in the B40 and M40 groups who are in need, through the Uyarvu Madani programme following the extraordinary response to applications for the programme. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the government will also examine other sources of financing, including collaboration through other agencies, to help more entrepreneurs expand their businesses. “We received 8,368 applications for Uyarvu Madani, but we can only grant it to about 780 recipients.

items.title: MMEA officer killed, two injured during operation in Kuala Perlis waters
items.summary: Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed that the incident occurred yesterday at around 11 pm, however, he said that further information regarding the incident can only be released by the MMEA. “I can only confirm receiving the report of this incident, but further information regarding this incident can only be released by the MMEA,” he said. — Bernama

items.title: Sarawak Assembly dissolution notification sent to EC, says Speaker
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 27 — A notification letter on the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly has been sent to the Election Commission (EC) today, said Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar. He said he had received the declaration of the dissolution of the state assemby, signed by Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar on Friday (Oct 23) “The declaration of dissolution is also in accordance with Article 21(2) of the State Constitution, which empowers the Governor of Sarawak to dissolve the state assembly. On Oct 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the State Legislative Assembly would be dissolved on Monday (Oct 26), paving the way for the 13th state election.

items.title: Anwar defends bigger development allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, cites infrastructure needs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government has defended its decision to provide larger development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak, citing their geographical challenges and infrastructure needs. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said these needs included the poor condition of roads in several areas of Sabah, despite its smaller population compared with other states. In response, Anwar said the development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak announced in Budget 2027 did not include expenditure for the projects under KKDW raised by the MP.

items.title: Anwar calls for stricter rules for GLCs, says bosses must not treat them as family property
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is considering a Government-Owned Entities Bill to tighten governance at government-linked companies (GLCs) and related agencies, and prevent misappropriation such as that seen in 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), Felda and Tabung Haji. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the proposed law would set clearer rules and ensure government-owned entities, including their subsidiaries, were subject to effective oversight. Instead, investment decisions must be made by investment bodies comprising professionals and people with relevant expertise, he said.

items.title: Anwar plans new law for GLCs and GLICs, cites Battersea losses and eFishery failure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government plans to introduce legislation to tighten governance at government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said clear rules were also needed for subsidiaries of government agencies, adding that the government had not identified governance breaches on the scale previously seen at 1MDB and Tabung Haji. Anwar said investments by GLICs and GLCs helped local companies expand and attract private investment from domestic and foreign investors.

items.title: RM1,000 per attack? Perak police arrest three teens over arson, paint-splashing cases across four states
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said Taiping police arrested the three men at separate locations in Penang between 5pm and 9pm on October 22, and had helped solve nine vandalism cases across four states: two in Perak, three in Kedah, two in Johor, one in Penang and one in Selangor. “The second suspect, a storekeeper, was arrested in Taman Sri Rambai, Bukit Mertajam, where police seized a mobile phone, clothing and a white Nissan Teana. Police are investigating two cases in Taiping.

items.title: Love is in the air, and so is the bill: 13pc of Malaysian men willing to go into debt for dates
items.summary: According to research by Legasi Research, men continue to shoulder most dating expenses, with 59.3 per cent saying they usually pay the entire bill, compared with just 8.2 per cent of women. Dinner dates and the price of romance Shopping malls remain a popular dating destination, with 44.1 per cent of respondents saying they frequent them, while 42.8 per cent opt for cafes or restaurants. Men also appear more likely to feel the financial strain, with 27.5 per cent reporting pressure from dating expenses, compared with 16.4 per cent of women.

items.title: Transferred Perak principal now under police probe after mother reports alleged sexual harassment of her Form Three daughter
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 27 — Police are investigating alleged sexual harassment involving a school principal and a Form Three student in Hutan Melintang, Perak, following a report by the student’s mother. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the report was lodged on October 24, with the case being investigated under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. “Following the report lodged by the victim’s mother, the case is being investigated under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters today.

items.title: Anwar defends GLIC-funded housing, says Petronas helped develop Putrajaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today defended the use of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to fund domestic development, citing Petronas’ role in Putrajaya and arguing that public needs can be balanced with commercial returns. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said that the national oil company had helped fund Putrajaya’s development through Putrajaya Holdings, which encompasses government offices, public amenities, hotels, commercial ventures and tourism facilities. Anwar said the first phase of a student accommodation initiative would involve 10,000 units, with a longer-term target of 30,000 units involving GLICs.
